title: Alcaraz's Big Comeback Sends Jodar to the ATP Finals
summary:
Carlos Alcaraz saved two match points and fought back to beat Taylor Fritz 6-7 (10-12), 7-5, 6-3 on Friday, November 6. The win sent Alcaraz into the semi-finals, and it also booked a place at the ATP Finals for 20-year-old Spaniard Jodar.

Fritz won a tight first set in a tie-break. Then he moved a break ahead in the second set, and the match looked lost for Alcaraz. But the 23-year-old Spaniard refused to give up. He saved two match points, broke Fritz twice, and tied the match. Then he took charge, moving 3-1 ahead in the final set and finishing with a powerful forehand. 'I tried not to let myself down in those difficult moments, to stay strong mentally,' Alcaraz said.

Alcaraz will face either Casper Ruud or Nuno Borges in the semi-finals. Jodar's place at the finals in Turin, Italy, is now safe. The event, held from November 15 to 22, features the top eight men's singles players in the world. Jodar will make his debut there, as will American Frances Tiafoe, 28.

Jodar only became a full-time professional at the start of 2026. The Madrid-born youngster won three ATP Challenger titles in 2025 and claimed his first ATP Tour title in Marrakech in April 2026.
why_it_matters: It shows that staying calm and never giving up can turn a hard game around, just like when you keep trying at school or in sport even when you are losing.
